t: A Hausa kingdom centred on the walled city of Kano, ruled by 43 kings from Bagauda, dated to 999, to the Fulani jihad.
Muhammad Rumfa (1463–1499) built the Gidan Rumfa, founded the Kurmi market and took advice on Islamic rule from al-Maghili.
Indigo-dyed cloth, leather, kola and the caravan trade made Kano the leading market city of the central Sudan.
dyk: According to the Kano Chronicle, cowrie shells, later the everyday small change of Hausaland, first reached the region in the reign of Muhammad Sharefa (1703–1731).
ev: Bagauda becomes the first king of Kano, by the Kano Chronicle’s reckoning
Under Yaji, Wangara Muslims from Mali bring Islam to the Kano court
Kanajeji equips his cavalry with quilted armour, iron helmets and coats of mail
Abdullahi Burja pays tribute to Bornu and opens trade roads to Gonja
Muhammad Rumfa becomes king; he builds the Gidan Rumfa and founds the Kurmi market
Kwararafa (Jukun) forces break into Kano and the king flees to Daura
Muhammad Alwali II, the last Hausa king of Kano, comes to the throne
The Fulani jihad reaches Kano; Alwali is later driven out and killed at Burum-Burum

f.founder: Bagauda, according to the Kano Chronicle
f.predecessor: Communities around Dala hill and neighbouring chiefdoms such as Santolo
